notes: The run is substantively strong: specs are accurate against the code (every one of 27 items verified), behavioral, cross-linked, and the executor even ran the CLI and surfaced a real contract gap (unknown --priority escapes as a traceback). The only failure is the prose lint at 78 findings, which is also the only assertion that distinguishes old-skill from new-skill output here, so the suite is well targeted but thin on style: nothing checks the 'load when' hints or doc-index quality beyond link presence. Two assertion wording issues: (a) the placeholder assertion says 'HTML comment blocks of template tips', while check_run.py flags any HTML comment, so a legitimate dated TODO comment (which the old skill's own process rule prescribes) trips the script but not the assertion; decide which is intended and align them. (b) The invariants assertion asks for 'one of them' to capture append-only plus single-source-of-truth, but a good writer naturally splits these into two invariants (as here); rewording to 'the invariants capture...' would avoid penalizing the better structure. The 'specs match the code' assertion is solid but could add one CLI-level fact (exit code 2 on rejection) to cover the cli.md file, which currently has no code-matching check.
